topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session by connecting histopathology practical observations to cellular transformation and outlining the core learning objectives.

topics.label: Tumor virology and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays to assess cell transformation.

topics.label: Oncogenes, tumor suppressors, and mutation mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the functional definitions and genetic mechanisms distinguishing oncogenes from tumor suppressor genes, using cell-cycle regulators and dosage effects as key models.

topics.label: Mechanisms of sequence and chromosomal genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how defects in specific DNA repair pathways, replication machinery, and mitotic chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how stepwise mutation accumulation and inherited gene defects drive cancer progression and affect tumor evolution.

topics.label: Conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, provides a recommended reading resource, and previews the next lecture on the hallmarks of cancer.
